profile.reading: This OpenStreetMap record at 10801 Bush Lake Road in Bloomington, Minnesota, part of the Minneapolis metro area, is tagged telecom=data_center and named "Verizon - Bloomington Network." Reviewing the record's own OpenStreetMap edit history shows the building carried no identifying tags at all from 2011 until April 2026, when a single contributor added an operator tag for Verizon and a phone number, citing only self-reported "local knowledge" rather than any independently verifiable source, then added the data-center tag itself in a separate edit minutes later with no further sourcing. This makes the underlying map data considerably less established than it might first appear, a single, unsourced, and quite recent contribution rather than long-standing, multiply-verified information. Verizon Communications is a real, major telecommunications company, but Minnesota's legacy local telephone territory was served historically by Contel of Minnesota, a GTE subsidiary whose properties were largely sold off to Frontier Communications by 2010, meaning this cannot represent a currently Verizon-operated legacy central office. If a Verizon facility genuinely exists at this address, Verizon Wireless network infrastructure, such as a mobile switching facility supporting nationwide cellular service, is the more plausible category, though this remains inference rather than a confirmed fact, since no independent news coverage, county property record, or FCC filing could be located this session because search-tool quota was exhausted. This entry is filed as an honest, unresolved case rather than asserting fabricated data-center specifications for what the underlying source data itself only weakly supports.

sources.title: Equinix Completes Acquisition of 29 Data Centers from Verizon

profile.research_note: Verizon sold its commercial colocation/data-center business (29 facilities) to Equinix in 2017 and exited the public colocation market; it does not publish colocation spec sheets. These rows are Verizon-operated network facilities (switching centers, wireless MSC/central-office buildings) rather than for-lease colocation space, and no public technical spec page exists for them. Marked specs_unpublished rather than guess.

reading.body:
This facility's capacity is not published. The record in OpenStreetMap dates to April 2026 and rests on a single unsourced contributor's addition of Verizon as operator and a data center tag, with no independent verification from news coverage, property records, or regulatory filings. Verizon divested its commercial colocation business entirely in 2017 when it sold 29 data centers to Equinix, meaning any Verizon facility at this address would be internal network infrastructure rather than for-lease AI compute capacity.

If the facility exists as identified, it most likely serves as a mobile switching center or network switching facility supporting Verizon Wireless operations rather than a data center hosting external tenants. No technical specifications are published for such facilities, and no independent source has confirmed either the facility's existence or its function at this address.

Minnesota has 13 mapped data center facilities with only 2 publishing power capacity figures totaling 10 MW. This facility cannot be ranked against published state capacity because its power draw is not disclosed and its operational status remains unconfirmed. It does not qualify as an established part of Minnesota's mapped AI infrastructure.
